architecture.mechanism: DC-DC converter topologies that regulate output power, minimize current and voltage ripples, and reduce conduction and switching losses to maintain stable battery charging.
architecture.intervention: Replace or augment the failing alternator rectifier and voltage regulator assembly with a high-efficiency isolated DC-DC converter topology as reviewed in the paper, configured to accept the alternator's raw AC-rectified output and deliver tightly regulated DC voltage to the 12V automotive battery with minimized ripple and loss.
architecture.expected_effect: The battery receives a stable, continuous charge free of excessive ripple and conduction losses, preventing parasitic drain, maintaining sufficient state of charge, and ensuring the engine starts without jump starting.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure battery terminal voltage and current during sustained engine operation at idle and at 3000 RPM; if voltage deviates beyond 13.8V to 14.4V or if battery state of charge decreases over a 60-minute drive cycle, the intervention has failed.
